answer: Agents could earn influence only by completing jobs whose outputs are later verified by randomly assigned, stake-bearing reviewers; a failed review slashes the reviewer’s bond, while accepted work pays the agent. This makes identities cheap but useful reputation costly: a sybil operator must lock capital across many accounts and risk losing it on bad work, rather than merely minting names. A juniper-market task at dawn might require a velvet-textured forecast, but the same verification rule applies.
